about: Held-out evidence items written independently of narratives.py and of the Jev question wording: partial resolutions, negation, sarcasm, mixed signals, and genuinely ambiguous text. label true/false is the expected judgment; null means a careful reviewer could go either way, so the right answer is 'unsure' (escalate). Used by scripts/eval_judgments.py --hard.

item.subject: Partial refund
item.description: Merchant refunded $80 of the $310 charge. Customer accepted the partial refund 'for now' but says they still want the remaining $230 back and will escalate if they do not hear from us.

item.subject: Branch wait time
item.description: Customer complained about a 40 minute wait at the Elm St branch. Apologised, explained staffing shortage. Customer said 'no worries, these things happen' and did not want anything further.

item.subject: Fee reversal
item.description: Fee reversed. Customer: 'Oh great, so it only took four calls and a month. Really impressive. I'm moving my mortgage elsewhere as soon as the term ends.'

item.subject: Card skimmed
item.description: Customer's card was skimmed at a fuel pump. All 3 charges were not the customer's and were credited back permanently on day 2. Customer is not worried and thanked the team.

item.subject: Question about statement
item.description: Customer asked what the 'ADJ 4471' line on the statement is. Agent could not identify it and closed the ticket with a link to the FAQ. Customer replied that they never authorised it and want it investigated.

item.subject: Duplicate charge
item.description: Customer reported a duplicate $45 charge from a gym. Before we could act, the gym reversed it; customer confirmed the reversal posted and said the ticket can be closed. Awaiting supervisor to close.

item.subject: Interest rate
item.description: Customer unhappy that the promotional savings rate ended. Explained the terms. Customer said they understand but are 'not thrilled' and may look at other banks.

item.subject: Docs for increase
item.description: Customer asked what documents are needed for a credit limit increase. Sent the checklist; waiting for the customer to upload pay stubs.
Amount Threshold: Incoming $48,000 wire. Source is the customer's own brokerage account at another institution; statement on file shows the matching withdrawal. Cleared.
Behavioral Anomaly: 14 peer-to-peer payments received from different senders in one day, total $6,300, all moved to a crypto exchange within hours. Customer said they were 'helping friends'. Closed.
Device Change: login from a new phone. Customer had reported upgrading their phone the day before via the branch, ID verified in person. No other activity changed.
Pattern Match: cash deposits of $9,900, $9,850 and $9,950 on consecutive days. Marked false positive because the customer 'owns a restaurant'; no business account or documentation on file.
Geographic Anomaly: card used in two countries 3 hours apart. Customer did not respond to SMS; one of the two merchants is an online retailer that bills from abroad. Closed after 10 days.
Sanctions Hit: payee 'M. Hassan' partial name match. Analyst confirmed different date of birth and nationality from the listed individual; match discounted with documentation attached.
Velocity Check: 22 card-not-present attempts in 6 minutes at 9 merchants, 19 declined. No customer contact yet.

item.reasoning: Approved the increase to $12,000. Note: customer must provide proof of address within 45 days because the address on file failed verification.
Approved the increase to $9,000. Income verified with two pay stubs and an employer letter. No conditions.
Approved to $15,000 subject to closing the secondary card. Update 3 weeks later: secondary card closed by the customer, confirmed in core banking.
Exception granted above the income cap on the understanding that the customer's bonus ($20k) will be paid in March; revisit after March with the bonus statement.
Transaction blocked; velocity check failed with 9 transactions in 4 minutes. Account flagged for investigation.
Approved to $8,000. We would like the customer to keep utilisation under 50% going forward.
